Report Verbs with Impersonal Passive Constructions
You can use the structure: It + passive report verb + finite clause (a clause which can stand alone) to report information.
For example:
It is thought that the Pyramids took 25 years to build.
This pattern is often used in formal reports, news reports and academic writing.

images.text: Depending on the purpose of the team, it is believed that some team roles may not be required so the absence of a particular role is not necessarily a cause for concern. For example, if the team has been given parameters to work within for a new ad campaign which needs to be created. It is supposed that including a Plant on the team would be counter-productive, in that they may want to come up with something new altogether and not work within the constraints.

Since there can be missing team roles, there may be times in a project where that role is required. It is worth considering how that gap can be filled, can someone in the team fulfil the role or should someone else be brought in to provide a specific contribution?</br>There may be gaps and overlaps in team roles because most people will fit into more than one team role. It is recommended that some roles are better in smaller doses. A large number of Plants in a team may cause too many ideas competing to be praised and too many Shapers can lead to aggressive behaviour.

Too many Specialists may become territorial, whereas an over supply of Completer Finishers may step on each other's toes, looking for the final “sign‐off” on a piece of work. As team roles can be grouped into thinking, social and action-oriented roles, all three areas should be well represented, but again, the purpose of the team is important. It is understood that there are times when social roles may not be as necessary as thinking and action roles or vice versa. It is known that there is no right or wrong way to form a team.
